 Glenn Maxwell retires from international cricket, brings curtain down on 14-year career
 Glenn Maxwell has retired from international cricket, bringing an end to a 14-year Australia career across all three formats. The explosive all-rounder leaves behind a remarkable legacy, headlined by his unforgettable 201* against Afghanistan in the 2023 ODI World Cup.
 Advertisement Glenn Maxwell has retired from international cricket. Courtesy: PTI By: India Today Sports Desk New Delhi , Nov 3, 2026 00:23 IST Last Updated Nov 3, 2026 00:23 IST Published by sabyasachi chowdhury Nov 3, 2026 00:17 IST Written By Sabyasachi Chowdhury Glenn Maxwell has announced his retirement from international cricket, bringing the curtain down on a remarkable 14-year career with Australia, Cricinfo reported. One of the most destructive and unconventional batters of his generation, Maxwell leaves behind a legacy built on breathtaking strokeplay, match-winning performances and an ability to turn games around almost single-handedly.
 The 38-year-old represented Australia across all three formats, playing seven Tests, 149 One-Day Internationals and 130 T20 Internationals. He scored 3,990 runs in ODIs, 2,897 in T20Is and 339 in Test cricket. He also claimed 136 international wickets, establishing himself as a valuable all-round option in Australia's white-ball teams. MAXWELL SHINES IN EXPLOSIVE CAREER
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Maxwell's international journey began with his ODI debut against Afghanistan in Sharjah on August 25, 2012. He made his T20I debut against Pakistan in Dubai in September that year before earning his Test cap against India in Hyderabad in March 2013.
 His career featured two ODI World Cup triumphs, in 2015 and 2023, as well as the T20 World Cup title in 2021. However, it was his extraordinary innings against Afghanistan during the 2023 ODI World Cup that came to define his career.
 At the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai, Australia were chasing 292 and appeared to be heading towards defeat after slipping to 91 for seven. Maxwell, battling severe cramps and struggling to move freely, produced one of the greatest rescue acts in ODI history.
 He remained unbeaten on 201 off just 128 deliveries , striking 21 fours and 10 sixes. Alongside Pat Cummins, who made an unbeaten 12, Maxwell put together an unbroken 202-run partnership to take Australia home with three wickets and 19 balls to spare.
 Maxwell repeatedly struggled with cramps, at times barely able to stand, but continued to find ways to score runs. His double century was the first by an Australian men's batter in ODI cricket and helped keep Australia's campaign alive. They went on to win the tournament, beating India in the final. MAXWELL MISSES OUT ON AUSTRALIA'S CENTRAL CONTRACT
 The signs of Maxwell's diminishing involvement in Australia's international plans had become increasingly apparent in 2026. Cricket Australia left him out of its national central contract list for the 2026-27 season, announced in April.
 His omission came after his ODI retirement and amid uncertainty over his long-term international future. The decision was part of a wider shift in Australia's contract list as the selectors planned for a demanding international schedule.
 Maxwell had already announced his retirement from ODI cricket in June 2025 , with his final appearance in the format coming against India in the Champions Trophy semi-final in Dubai. The physical demands of the format and the toll of repeated injuries influenced his decision.
 His absence from the central contract list did not automatically mean the end of his T20I career. Maxwell had indicated earlier in March that he was not ready to make a formal decision on his future in the shortest format. He wanted to assess his fitness and form while keeping the possibility of representing Australia again open. BANGLADESH TOUR OMISSION PRECEDED RETIREMENT
 Maxwell was also left out of Australia's T20I squad for the tour of Bangladesh in May-June 2026. The selectors opted for a new-look group, with Maxwell, Steve Smith and Marcus Stoinis among the experienced players overlooked.
 The omission attracted attention, although chief selector George Bailey indicated at the time that the trio's T20I careers were not necessarily over. Maxwell's final international appearance came against Oman in Australia's T20 World Cup Super Eights clash on February 20, 2026.
 With his international career now over, Australia lose a player whose ability to produce extraordinary moments made him one of the most entertaining cricketers of his era.
 While Maxwell is stepping away from international cricket, his franchise career remains a separate chapter. He has continued to feature in T20 leagues around the world and remains contracted to Melbourne Stars in the Big Bash League until the end of the 2026-27 season.
 For Australia, however, the announcement marks the end of an era. Maxwell's numbers tell part of the story, but his legacy will be remembered most vividly through the moments when he made the extraordinary look possible. - Ends
